You can incrementally "fit" a dataset, allowing you to iterate slowly through the learning process of the kmeans algorithm
Click this several times while looking at the plot. Notice how the clustering slightly shifts each time as the algorithm learns a more optimal clustering.
The colour denotes which cluster the point belongs to.
You can also "set" the means from which kmeans will learn clusters. With low iteration counts, this allows you to bias the clustering process

You will notice that after one interation, the space is roughly around the 4 means that were set in step 2.

This means that we can "seed" kmeans to find certain clusters rather than letting it come to its own conclusions from a random starting point.
fluid.kmeans~ can converge on similar clustering even with extreme means set as the seed. By keeping the iterations low it is more obvious how it affects the clustering process.
Then fitpredict to predict the cluster for each point based on the means we provided.
